entities.summary: Wang Chong, courtesy name Zhongren (仲任), was a Chinese astronomer, meteorologist, naturalist, philosopher, and writer active during the Eastern Han dynasty. He developed a rational, secular, naturalistic and mechanistic account of the world and of human beings and gave a materialistic explanation of the origin of the universe. His main work was the Lunheng. This book contained many theories involving early sciences of astronomy and meteorology, and Wang Chong was even the first in Chinese history to mention the use of the square-pallet chain pump, which became common in irrigation and public works in China thereafter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wang Chong's work in Lunheng laid foundational principles for Chinese scientific inquiry and irrigation engineering, influencing subsequent generations of scholars and engineers. His theories on meteorology and astronomy also contributed to the development of early Chinese science.
